programs.name: Totally Disabled Veteran Full Exemption (IC 6-1.1-12-14, HEA 1210-2026)

type.quote: Section 14 provides a deduction equal to 100% of the assessed value of real property, a mobile home ... Beginning with the 2026 assessment date (2026 Pay 2027), there is no maximum assessed value

ratingRequired.quote: IC 6-1.1-12-14 does not state that the veteran's total disability must be service-connected. Section 14 requires a total disability evidenced by a VA pension certificate or award of compensation, or an IDVA certificate of eligibility.
ratingRequired.note: Total disability need NOT be service-connected (VA pension suffices). Also requires 90+ days service, honorable discharge, and one year of Indiana residency before the assessment date; trusts are not eligible (FAQ Q3).

survivingSpouse.quote: if the veteran satisfied IC 6-1.1-12-14(a)(1) through (a)(4) at the time of death and the surviving spouse owns or is buying the property

programs.effectiveChanges: Effective 2026 assessment date (2026-pay-2027 bills). Transition: anyone who held the old $14,000 deduction is auto-converted to the $250 credit and 'must file a new application to receive the amended 100% deduction' (Form 12662 R20/6-26) by January 15, 2027. Receiving the 100% deduction bars the $250/$350 credits (IC 6-1.1-12-14(d)).
programs.note: Deduction covers the homestead parcel only (FAQ Q6: not property that is not part of or used with the home).

programs.name: Wartime Disabled Veteran Credit (IC 6-1.1-51.3-6)

exemptionValue.quote: $350 Service-Connected Disability Credit (IC § 6-1.1-51.3-6) ... have a service-connected disability of at least 10%.

wartimeRequired.quote: Wartime service is not required for the 100% deduction under IC 6-1.1-12-14, and it is not required for the $250 credit under IC 6-1.1-51.3-5. The $350 credit ...

survivingSpouse.quote: For the $350 credit, the deceased veteran must have satisfied IC 6-1.1-51.3-6(a)(1) through (a)(4) at death, and the surviving spouse must satisfy the ownership or qualifying-contract requirement

programs.effectiveChanges: 2026-pay-2027: DLGF recommends counties auto-convert the former $24,960 deduction to the $350 credit; no Indiana-residency requirement; credit may be split across properties; unused credit is not refunded or carried.

programs.name: Deduction for Property Received from Tax Exempt Organization

ratingRequired.quote: Form 12662 Section V (IC 6-1.1-12-14.5): deduction equal to the veteran's disability percentage of assessed value for a homestead donated by a 501(c)(3); requires 90 days service, honorable discharge, 50%+ rating (per filing-layer read of the form).
ratingRequired.note: DLGF 5/27/2026 memo table lists 'Deduction for Homestead Donated to Veteran' and bars combining it with the 100% deduction ('A person may not claim this deduction with the Deduction for Homestead Donated to Veteran').

summary.correct: Homestead donated at no charge by a 501(c)(3): deduction equals the veteran's VA disability percentage (50% to 100%) of assessed value (IC 6-1.1-12-14.5). Rare; not combinable with the 100% total-disability deduction.
summary.quote: A person may not claim this deduction with the Deduction for Homestead Donated to Veteran.

programs.note: Niche program; should not be added to a typical rated veteran's savings.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran 62+ Credit (IC 6-1.1-51.3-5)

survivingSpouse.quote: For the $250 credit, a surviving spouse may qualify if the deceased veteran satisfied IC 6-1.1-51.3-5(a)(1) through (a)(4) at death
survivingSpouse.note: Filing layer adds: also if the veteran was killed in action, died on active duty, or died during inactive duty training.

minAge.quote: A 33-year old veteran with a 10% disability does not qualify for the $250 credit because IC 6-1.1-51.3-5 requires the veteran to be at least 62 years old.

programs.effectiveChanges: 2026-pay-2027: applied automatically (one-time) to anyone converted from the old $14,000 deduction; the $250 and $350 credits may be combined with each other but not with the 100% deduction.

jurisdictionNote.correct: HEA 1210-2026 (effective the Jan 1, 2026 assessment date, 2026-pay-2027 bills) replaced the old deductions ($24,960 wartime; $14,000 total disability/62+; $240K home cap) with: a 100% deduction of assessed value for totally disabled veterans (no service-connection or value cap; one year Indiana residency; no trusts), a $350 credit for wartime veterans rated 10%+, and a $250 credit for veterans 62+ rated 10%+. The credits stack with each other but not with the 100% deduction. New Form 12662 due January 15; veterans converted from the old $14,000 deduction must refile by Jan 15, 2027.
